Leaf removal

Leaf removal that actually finishes the job

Leaves are the reason most people book a fall cleanup, and they’re also the part that’s easiest to get half-right. Blowing leaves into a pile at the curb, or raking the lawn but leaving the beds packed, just moves the problem. A proper leaf removal clears the turf, pulls leaves out from under shrubs and out of garden beds, and gets them off hard surfaces where wet leaves turn slippery.

Then they have to go somewhere. We bag leaves for municipal yard-waste collection or haul them away with us — you pick at quoting. Either way, nothing gets left in a corner of your yard.

Not every lawn needs every leaf removed. A light scattering can be mulched straight into the grass with a mower, and that feeds the soil. Heavy cover is different: under a big maple or oak it compacts into a wet mat over winter that smothers grass and invites snow mould. We’ll tell you which you have rather than sell you a bigger job than you need.

Local know-how

Fall cleanup in Guelph

Guelph is a city of mature trees. Older neighbourhoods like Old University, Exhibition Park and Riverside Park have big street maples and oaks, and even newer south-end streets in Kortright, Westminster Woods and Clairfields now drop a serious volume of leaves. Oaks and some maples hold onto their leaves well into November, which is why one early rake rarely does it.

Timing. The best fall yard cleanup happens once most of the canopy is down but before the ground freezes — typically late October into November in Guelph. We watch conditions across our route and schedule each cleanup when the yard is actually ready, not on an arbitrary date.

Preparing the lawn for winter. The final cut of the year goes slightly lower than our usual 3-inch summer height — around 2.5 inches. That’s short enough to resist matting and snow mould, tall enough to protect the crown of the grass. Clearing the leaves off at the same time means the turf goes into winter able to breathe.

Garden beds. Clearing spent annuals, fallen leaves and debris out of beds now saves a messier job in April, and keeps beds from becoming a winter hiding spot for pests.

Getting rid of the waste. The City of Guelph doesn’t accept leaves or yard waste in the green cart, and its curbside loose-leaf and yard-waste collection runs on set dates that change from year to year. The City also asks residents not to rake leaves onto the road, where they block bike lanes and storm drains. Because we bag or haul everything ourselves, your cleanup isn’t tied to the collection calendar.

Township of Puslinch

Fall cleanup in Puslinch

Just south of Guelph, the Township of Puslinch — including Aberfoyle, Morriston, Arkell and the homes around Puslinch Lake — is a different kind of fall clean-up. Lots are bigger, many back onto woodlots or hedgerows, and long driveways and wide lawns collect far more leaves than a typical city yard.

  • Quoted per property. Acreage and tree cover vary too much for a one-size price, so every Puslinch quote is based on your actual lot.
  • Haul-away matters more. Leaf and yard-waste collection in Puslinch is run by the County of Wellington, not the City of Guelph, and curbside pickup doesn’t reach every rural address. Taking the material with us is often the simplest option.
  • Tell us what’s underfoot. If you have a septic bed, well cap or soft low spot on the lawn, let us know when you book so we work around it.

Common questions

Fall cleanup FAQ

How much does fall cleanup cost in Guelph?

Every fall cleanup is quoted on your actual property, because two yards on the same street can be very different jobs. What moves the price: lot size, how many mature trees drop leaves on it, how much bed space needs clearing, and how much material has to be hauled away. Send your address through the quote form and you’ll get a firm price within 24 hours — no contract attached.

When should I schedule fall cleanup?

Book in early to mid-October and plan for the cleanup itself to happen once most of your trees are bare — in Guelph that’s usually late October into November. Too early and the yard is covered again a week later; too late and you’re dealing with frozen, matted leaves or snow.

Does Yardex remove leaves?

Yes. Leaf removal is the core of every fall cleanup: we clear leaves from the lawn, out of garden beds and off driveways and walkways, then bag them for yard-waste pickup or haul them away — your choice at quoting. If your leaf cover is light enough to mulch into the lawn instead, we’ll tell you.

Do you provide fall cleanup in Puslinch?

Yes. We do fall cleanups in the Township of Puslinch as well as across Guelph. Puslinch properties tend to be larger and more wooded, so we quote them individually — and because curbside yard-waste collection doesn’t reach every rural address, haul-away is often the most practical option there.

Can I book a one-time fall cleanup?

Absolutely. A fall cleanup is a standalone, one-time service — you don’t need weekly mowing with us and there’s no contract or cancellation fee. Plenty of clients start with a cleanup and come back for spring cleanup or weekly mowing the next season.

What does fall cleanup include?

Leaf and debris removal from the lawn, beds and hard surfaces; garden beds cleared out and tidied; edges re-defined; a final cut of the season at around 2.5 inches; and everything we collect bagged or hauled away. Your written quote spells out exactly what’s included for your property.

Is it okay to just mulch my leaves into the lawn?

For a light layer, yes — mowing a thin cover of leaves into the turf is healthy. Under mature maples and oaks the cover is usually too heavy; it mats down under snow and leaves dead patches in April. We’ll tell you honestly which side of that line your yard is on.
